## Session Report

* [H-A2 report: every all-boson vertex of self-conjugate legs takes (−1)^{n_P} against MadGraph](H-A2-report.md) - The momentum sign MadGraph's all-outgoing reading puts on a vertex against vibegraph's all-incoming one was applied only to coloured three-vector vertices. It now applies to every all-boson vertex whose legs are all self-conjugate: −1 iff its Lorentz terms carry an odd number of momenta; a vertex whose terms disagree on the parity is refused. Four new standalone JAMP rows (O_HG's and O_HGtil's Higgs-three-gluon contacts, O_HG's Higgs-four-gluon contact, O_G's five-gluon contact) agree with MadGraph to ≤ 1.2e-15 and all fail with the three-leg restriction back. σ, grids and events of three cards without such a vertex are bit for bit. TCP_m50/m55 over five seeds: σ/MG 1.007 ± 0.010 and 1.025 ± 0.008, identical to the last bit to the diagnostic trial; the m55 2.7σ residual is not explained here.
* [H-C1 report: xpt* at or below zero, and the per-PDG pT minimum](H-C1-report.md) - xptj/xptb/xpta/xptl ≤ 0 read as off; pt_min_pdg applied as setcuts.f applies it, with MadGraph's refusals; two MadGraph defects found (the light-PDG refusal never fires; the setcuts.f:681 smin loop index removes phase space on some cards), local MadGraph σ against vibegraph, mutation evidence, the M3 banking request and Found.
* [H-C2 report: MadEvent's cut_decays exemption cannot be reproduced on an every-pairing |M|²](H-C2-report.md) - Stopped before code, as the brief allows. With every pairing kept in |M|², exempting MadGraph's pairing's decay legs leaves uncut a leg that is a core quark in another kept pairing. That quark carries the t-channel collinear singularity, so σ diverges: on g g > z u u~, z > u u~ the integrand at a point that passes the exempted cuts and the window union grows as 1/pT² of the exempt quark over three decades (value·pT² = 5.15e-18 constant to 4%), a logarithmic divergence of σ. MadEvent is finite only because its |M|² is the single pairing. An honest reproduction needs per-pairing |M|²: compat site (d), or a pairing-weighted cut. The user's call.
* [H-C3 report: an IR-unsafe cut_decays exemption is refused; the every-pairing rule registered](H-C3-report.md) - Cuts::compile_with refuses an exemption from the cuts that leaves uncut a massless coloured leg which is a core parton in some kept diagram (CutError::IrUnsafeExemption). Today's every-pairing rule never produces one, and the guard is bit for bit on two decay-chain cards and one plain card (σ, grid and events SHA-256). Its unit test refuses MadEvent's configuration-1 mask on g g > z u u~, z > u u~, passes today's, and fails with the guard removed. The kb registers vibegraph's every-pairing rule as a deviation of its own cut: stricter than cut_decays = F asks, −26% / −6.8%, σ informational, with the kinematic window rule named as the intended fix. Compat site (g) is folded into site (d).
* [H-D1 report: MadGraph sums the two decay assignments of one subprocess incoherently; their interference is below 1e-3](H-D1-report.md) - On the pinned checkout, one subprocess reached by two disjoint decay assignments becomes two matrix elements (or two PDF terms of one), so MadEvent sums |M_a|² + |M_b|², each inside its own Breit–Wigner window; measured on p p > z j j, z > j j (30 such subprocesses, the same 30 vibegraph refuses, diagram totals equal). With vibegraph's own evaluators the interference is ≤ 1.4e-3 ± 1.1e-3 (colour-aligned e+ e-), 3.5e-4 (g g) and exactly 0 (q q̄ initial). A coherent sum differs from MadGraph mainly through the window union (+0.24% to +1.1%) and through cut_decays = F, where it moves σ by −23% to −26% or is IR-unsafe. Recommendation: match MadGraph. Neither option unblocks the hadronic cards alone: both then stop at the per-group cut-filter refusal.
* [H-D2 report: a subprocess reached by two decay assignments is two subprocesses, summed incoherently as MadGraph does](H-D2-report.md) - D3 implemented. The in-line DuplicateSubprocess refusal is gone; each (core, decay assignment) is its own DiagramSet with its own forced lines. The decay-chain census now banks g g / e+ e- / p p > z j j, z > j j and matches MadGraph's 6 / 6 / 30 doubly reached subprocesses with per-matrix-element diagram counts. σ of the twelve two-assignment subprocesses of g g > z j j, z > j j: 112.04 ± 0.06 pb (vibegraph) against 111.70 ± 0.18 pb (MadEvent), +0.30%, the same offset as a single-assignment calibration card (+0.32%), so the ratio agrees to −0.02%. No card that reaches the duplicate runs end to end through the CLI: every such card stops at GroupCutsDiffer (D4).
* [H-D3 report: the 11 duplicate-subprocess gridpacks against MadGraph; two decay assignments on two lines are two subprocesses too](H-D3-report.md) - MadGraph's generation of all 11 survey cards, measured on the pinned checkout: every flavour content two decay assignments reach is two (process, decays) entries, on one line (Zto2Q, Wto2Q, VLLD) or on two (Wto2Q's W+ and W- lines, TTToHcToWA, TpTp, VLLVLL). H-D2 lifted only the one-line case, so 7 of the 11 cards still stopped at the cross-line DuplicateSubprocess refusal. Two lines whose sets force different decay assignments are now kept as MadGraph keeps them; one assignment on two lines, or a decay chain and a plain line, stay refused. vibegraph's enumeration matches MadGraph's per-entry diagram counts and doubly reached contents on every BSM card (890 subprocesses, 417 doubly reached) and on the SM families' lines (Wto2Q only up to a leg-order difference on b̄-initial crossings). Census rows: the five-flavour Zto2Q line and two two-line SM cards. After enumeration the cards stop at GroupCutsDiffer (Zto2Q, Wto2Q, TTToHcToWA), massive incoming u (VLLD, VLLVLL, item 6) and a colour-basis split (TpTp).
* [H-G0 report: why crossing pairs refuse a shared colour basis](H-G0-report.md) - The charge-conjugate pairs have one basis up to a permutation, and the raw-order CF check refuses them before flow_permutation, which finds it, can run. The Singlet-model refusal is 184 zero-coupling b-Yukawa diagrams in the member.
* [H-G1 report: conjugate pairs share one flavour group under the flow permutation](H-G1-report.md) - The review of colour-split-groups, then the manager's scope update: colour_pairing takes π from the fingerprints and checks the CF matrix under π, so conjugate pairs form one group and only genuinely unpaired subprocesses (d d > d d / b b > b b at a zero b Yukawa) split. Mutations, the banked layer, and local MadGraph σ and per-subprocess colour-label oracles on a 2→3 pair and an HT-binned 12-flow pair; re-gated after merging main, with the σ oracle rerun on LHAPDF 247000, where a 1–2% offset survives the same PDF in single-subprocess controls.
* [H-J1 report: with no run card, maxjetflavor follows the incoming partons as in the card MadGraph writes](H-J1-report.md) - The absent-run-card default for a scattering process is now RunCard::scattering_default over the incoming PDG ids of the generated subprocesses (those with a diagram): maxjetflavor = max(4, heaviest incoming quark below 7) when an incoming parton is a quark up to b, a gluon or a photon, as banner.py's create_default_for_process writes it. asrwgtflavor is left at 5: MadGraph sets it in memory only, never writes it (a hidden parameter not in user_set), and reads back 5 at launch; the item's closes_when asked for both. MadGraph's own output cards give 5 for p p > j j and b b~ > z under sm-no_b_mass, 4 for p p > j j under sm and for p p > w+ under sm-no_b_mass. p p > j j under sm-no_b_mass with no run card: vibegraph 698.834 ± 0.263 µb against MadEvent (hard_survey = 2) 699.026 ± 0.298 µb, −2.7e-4, pull −0.48, five seeds each, chi2/dof 0.89 and 0.66; before the change the same card stopped at the CutIndicatorDiffers grouping refusal. Outgoing b quarks in both samples have pT ≥ 20 GeV and |eta| ≤ 5, at 1.69% and 1.66% of outgoing partons.
* [H-K1 report: per-group cut indicators, and cut agreement as a grouping join condition](H-K1-report.md) - D4 and item 8 implemented. A subprocess whose cut filter differs from a group's starts a group of its own (CutIndicatorDiffers is gone), and every flavour group carries its own cut indicator in ProtonIntegrand (GroupCutsDiffer is gone): a point's value is Σ_g Θ_g·term_g and its event is drawn among the passing groups. Every channel is built under the weakest of the groups' floors (UnionBounds): built under its own group's floors, the mixture read g g > z j j, z > j j 4% low, because a channel's density below its floors is positive. MadGraph refuses 5F p p > j j at maxjetflavor 4 whenever the b cuts differ from the jet cuts (setcuts.f consistency check), so the backlog item's 'MadGraph runs this card' holds only for equal b and jet cuts. σ: p p > j j at maxjetflavor 4 with ptb 30/etab 2.5 against MadGraph's three class-split runs, −6.1e-4, pull −0.98, five seeds each; g g > z j j, z > j j at cut_decays T +4.3e-3 (pull +2.7); at cut_decays F −6.8%, all of it in the four same-flavour subprocesses (an existing decay-product rule, Found); the twelve others agree to 1e-4. p p > j j j on the same card +3.0e-3 against MadGraph's four class-split runs (pull +2.3, the sign and size of MadEvent's known low reading). Cards with one filter are bit for bit, also on the merge with main. TTToHcToWA and both Wto2Q cards now integrate; Zto2Q stops on cost (11421 channels), not a refusal.

* [H-N1 report: near-degenerate flavour groups merge at rounding and split otherwise; the γ+jets split is the W width, not CP violation](H-N1-report.md) - D1 implemented: GROUP_REL_TOL 1e-10 → 1e-9 and the DegenerateGroups refusal (GROUP_SEPARATION_MIN) removed. Worst rounding-level separation over the banked proton cards and the survey reproductions is 1.48e-10 (p p > w- z j j QCD=0, the survey's 1.5e-10), identified by its f32/f64 scaling; the closest physical one is 1.2e-7. The 9.08e-7 u b~ / u~ b split is the reflection-odd part of |M|² carried by the W width: CP holds to 3e-16, the CKM phase moves the split only through |V_ub|. Every previously derivable partition unchanged; mutations caught; σ of p p > a j j QCD=0 against local MadGraph.
* [H-R1 report: the mirrored beam ordering now follows the proc card, as MadGraph's has_mirror_process does](H-R1-report.md) - Subprocess::has_mirror was incoming[0] != incoming[1], so a card written in one beam ordering was integrated in both: u u~ > e+ e- gave 1556.8 pb against MadGraph's 778.1, u g > u z 2877.0 against 1436.5. The enumeration now records, per subprocess, whether its own process line generated the exchanged ordering (MadGraph collects mirrors within one process definition only), and only then does the mirror term get luminosity. After the change the single-ordering rows match MadGraph at +4.8e-4 and +9.6e-4 (pulls +1.1, +1.0), both-orderings/single ratios are 1.99975 ± 0.00079 (MadGraph 2.00010 ± 0.00087) and 2.00166 ± 0.00112 (2.00088 ± 0.00205), every event of a single-ordering card has the card's parton on beam 1, and p p > e+ e- is bit for bit unchanged. Two lines writing the two orderings are now two unmirrored subprocesses (MadGraph's two P directories), not a refusal; at fixed-energy beams they are refused. The massive b b~ row waits for the massive-incoming branch.
